nodes.label: ADR 0012: Morphology generation is not Perl-parity-bound
nodes.rationale: Byte-for-byte parity with Tichý's create_dict31.pl was the right gate while porting, but the Perl script is no longer a usable product oracle and it encodes scholar bugs plus some historically wrong paradigms. Wright 1925 and related grammars outrank Tichý where they disagree. Unit tests and Python snapshots remain regression locks on current output; a snapshot diff is a prompt to say whether the change was meant, not a veto. This supersedes ADR 0009 Decision 7 while ADR 0009 class-shape work still stands.

nodes.label: create_dict31.pl
nodes.author: Tichý
nodes.rationale: The morphology generator began as a port of this Perl script. It is not a continuing oracle because it is not runnable as a product check here and it encodes bugs and some wrong paradigms.

nodes.label: Wright 1925 and related grammars
nodes.author: Wright
nodes.rationale: Historical grammars outrank Tichý where they disagree, so Wright-correct expansions such as class-II -ig-/-ige- spellings are in scope for the default generator when tests are updated with them.

nodes.label: ADR 0009 Decision 7: Perl as golden oracle
nodes.rationale: Decision 7 treated a diff against Perl as a parity regression, full stop. ADR 0012 supersedes that decision only; ADR 0009 class-shape work remains.

nodes.label: Python morphology regression snapshots
nodes.rationale: tests/morphology/parity_harness.py and related snapshots lock current Python output. They are not a Perl contract. A failing snapshot is not an automatic revert; intentional behavior changes update the snapshots in the same change.

nodes.label: morphology_perl_quirks_ledger.rst
nodes.rationale: The ledger is a catalog of inherited Tichý behaviors, not a do-not-fix list. Opt-in flags for every historical fix were the old quirks-ledger rule and were rejected so default output can become more correct.
